No source named contract months and no Brent second-month settle was found (value null); only MUFG's 5 Nov 'under USD 2.50/b' prompt spread. No Dated Brent / Dubai / EFS quote (Reuters physical item paywalled, date unconfirmed). Weekly Brent decline is printed variously as 12.5%, 13.3%, 16% and 17%. Transit measures conflict by an order of magnitude (PortWatch 1/day on 1 Nov; hormuz.now 3.1 AIS tankers/day; Windward 14 in 48h; UKMTO 325/week; ~31/day via Gulf News) - different definitions, none divided or reconciled. No current Hormuz mb/d flow figure (latest Kpler print is week to 29 Sep). War-risk % of hull: only an October 6-10% range, no November quote. UKMTO since-5-Nov count is a tally of press reports, not an official figure; UKMTO PDF, CENTCOM release, CNBC (3 URLs), straits.live 11-09 brief, invezz, Lloyd's List and US News were unreachable. Several sources (houseofsaud, straits.live, hormuz.now, financefeeds) are aggregators quoting others. Source weekday/date mismatches: Al Jazeera 8 Nov calls 7 Nov both Friday and Saturday; Qeshm strike night is 6 Nov per Al Jazeera 7 Nov. Mine-strike claims are IRGC-only and unconfirmed. items.note: Page prints Brent $98.32, up 3 cents on the day, Friday 6 Nov settle. Contract month NOT stated for the settle (same page calls the prior-Friday contract 'January Brent'). Corroborated: tradingeconomics 'previous close 98.32'; straits.live 'last settle $98.32, last print 6 Nov'; Business Recorder 09 Nov implies 98.32 (97.48 after -84c). DISAGREES with repo Yahoo continuous 97.76 and with cappnotes ~97.79.

items.name: Brent close (cappnotes Closing Look)
items.note: Page prints Brent 'about $97.79, -0.51%'; contract month not named. Close to repo Yahoo 97.76 but 53c below the 98.32 settle printed by CNBC/tradingeconomics/straits.live; sign of daily change also differs (-0.51% vs +3c). Likely a pre-settle snapshot; unresolved.

items.name: WTI front-month settle (CNBC via FinanceFeeds)
items.note: Page prints WTI $90.83, up 31 cents, Friday 6 Nov settle; contract month not stated. Business Recorder sidebar also lists crude $90.83 for Nov 6. DISAGREES with repo Yahoo continuous 90.34 and cappnotes ~90.37.

items.name: WTI close (cappnotes Closing Look)
items.note: Page prints WTI 'about $90.37, -0.17%'; contract month not named. Near repo Yahoo 90.34; 46c below the 90.83 printed by CNBC-derived sources.

items.name: Brent second-month settle
items.note: No page read printed a second-month Brent settle or named the contract months for 6 Nov. Only related print: MUFG 5 Nov daily said prompt Brent time spread 'under USD 2.50/b' vs more than USD 5/b mid-October (not a 6 Nov figure).

items.name: Prompt Brent time spread (MUFG, as described)
items.note: Printed only as a bound: prompt Brent time spread 'under USD 2.50/b' versus 'more than USD 5/b' in mid-October; Brent futures USD 94/b, WTI USD 87/b on that day's note. No exact value. Dated 5 Nov (at the gate, kept as latest structure print).

items.name: Dated Brent / Dubai physical
items.note: No dated physical quote obtained. The only physical-market page surfaced (Reuters 'Middle East Crude-Dubai slips for fourth session as Saudi Arabia to resume Yanbu exports') is paywalled, shows no price levels and its date could not be confirmed (it refers to the September East-West restart, so probably out of gate).

items.name: Brent intraday 01:38 GMT Monday (NOT a settle)
items.note: INTRADAY: Brent down 84 cents (0.85%) to $97.48 at 0138 GMT 9 Nov; contract month not stated. Says Brent fell 17% last week, steepest weekly drop since the pandemic, largest in absolute terms in LSEG data to 1988.

items.name: WTI intraday 01:38 GMT Monday (NOT a settle)
items.note: INTRADAY: WTI down 32 cents (0.35%) to $90.51 at 0138 GMT 9 Nov; contract month not stated.

items.name: Brent intraday 08:30 GMT Monday (NOT a settle)
items.note: INTRADAY: Brent down $1.65 (1.7%) to $96.67 as of 08:30 GMT; WTI down $0.96 (1%) to $89.87. Page says Brent fell 16% the previous week.

items.name: Brent intraday later Monday (tradingeconomics, NOT a settle)
items.note: INTRADAY: page says Brent 'fell to 95.06 USD/Bbl on November 9, 2026', -3.32% on the day; header ticker 94.941; previous close 98.32. Commentary cites overnight US strike on Qeshm, a tanker hit by projectile near Hormuz, Houthi damage to Aramco offices in Riyadh, and Gulf crude exports beginning to recover. Weekly decline printed inconsistently (13.3% vs 'over 12.5%'; Reuters copy says 17%, others 16%).

items.name: UKMTO weekly Hormuz transits (week to 4 Nov)
items.source: UKMTO weekly overview via Middle East Eye (7 Nov)
items.note: Printed as a weekly total: 325 transits vs 277 the previous week, about 65% below pre-conflict; roughly 80% energy carriers. Al Jazeera 7 Nov breaks it into 170 outbound and 155 inbound. No per-day figure printed (not divided here).

items.name: IMF PortWatch Hormuz transits (latest published day)
items.note: straits.live (page stamped 8 Nov 17:08Z): PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 1 Nov vs typical 85/day; flagged as contested, AIS-only, lagging. Conflicts in scale with UKMTO 325/week and with ~31/day 'early November, mostly US-escorted' (Gulf News via House of Saud).

items.name: AIS-visible tanker transits, 7-day average
items.note: Live figure as of 8 Nov: 3.1 AIS-visible tankers/day (7-day avg) vs 47.6 pre-crisis; all commercial ships 50 crossings in 7 days (22 in, 28 out); LNG/LPG carrier crossings 0 in 7 days, 1 LNG in 30 days. AIS floor.

items.name: Windward weekend Hormuz transits (18:00 UTC 6 Nov to 18:00 UTC 8 Nov)
items.note: 14 transits over the 48h window (8 inbound, 6 outbound), 8 of them dark. 7 Nov alone: 7 inbound (3 AIS-visible, 4 dark) and 4 outbound (1 visible, 3 dark) = 11; tankers 2 inbound, 1 outbound. Windward calls counts a floor. Gulf GPS jamming 6 Nov: 507 vessels.

items.name: Non-Iranian-linked Hormuz exits/entries (Breakwave)
items.note: Printed: eastbound exits fell to 43 from 67; westbound entries rose to 73 from 57 (non-Iranian-linked vessels; comparison period not stated in what was read, presumably week on week). MEG: 87 inbound VLCCs for 77 stems Friday.

items.name: Hormuz crude+products flow (latest printed estimate, STALE)
items.source: Kpler via CNN, as shown on hormuz.now
items.note: Latest flow estimate any page printed: 13.1 mb/d crude and products incl. dark ships, week to 29 Sep 2026 (just under 80% of 17.1 pre-war). NOT current; no November mb/d figure found. straits.live prints no current flow figure.

items.name: Gulf producer exports, October (MUFG)
items.source: MUFG Research Middle East Daily 5 Nov
items.note: October: Saudi crude exports ~7.0 mb/d (6.2 in Sep), Yanbu 3.1 mb/d; Iraq 3.4 (from 3.1); Kuwait 1.4; UAE 3.7 unchanged with weaker Fujairah; Iran no observed seaborne crude/condensate exports for a second month. Arab News 8 Nov prints Iraq ~3.5 mb/d in October vs 2.65 in September (differs).

items.name: Ras Laffan port calls (PortWatch via hormuz.now)
items.note: Port calls 1.2/day vs 4.8 before (24%), data to 30 Oct. QatarEnergy force majeure extends through November into early December (The National, 28 Sep). No in-gate Qatar LNG headline found.

items.name: Yanbu / Fujairah exports vs normal (PortWatch via hormuz.now)
items.note: Fujairah exports 78% of normal (data to 30 Oct). Same page prints Yanbu exports at '2% of normal' to 30 Oct, which conflicts with MUFG's Yanbu 3.1 mb/d for October; treat Yanbu figure as unreliable.

items.name: UKMTO weekly attacks (7 days to 4 Nov)
items.source: UKMTO weekly overview via Middle East Eye (7 Nov)
items.note: 11 commercial ships attacked: 8 in Hormuz, 3 in Arabian Gulf; 3 sank, 5 needed assistance, 3 continued. Al Jazeera 7 Nov words it as week ending 6 Nov. Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb: none (last 24 Aug).

items.name: UKMTO-reported incidents dated 5-8 Nov (count assembled from press, list in note)
items.source: Arab News / TASS / Maritime Executive / iMariner tracker
items.note: Individually reported: (1) 5 Nov outbound tanker, explosion at port waterline 16 nm E of Khasab, crew safe, continued; (2) 5 Nov tanker Velos Sapphire (Marshall Is.) hit by apparent projectile sailing empty to Bahrain (press, UKMTO attribution not explicit); (3) 7 Nov ~19:20 UTC tanker on fire 8 nm NW of Khasab, crew evacuated, OSINT tentatively Navig8 Messi; (4) 7 Nov tanker struck by unknown projectile outbound in Hormuz, crew safe = UKMTO advisory 200-26 ATTACK, dated 2026-11-08 by tracker (late report); (5) 7 Nov 21:32 GMT bulk carrier 'incident with military forces' 18 nm E of Khor Fakkan (appears to be the US strike on M/V Huda). Count of 5 is a tally of these press reports, not a UKMTO-printed number; Windward separately lists a 6 Nov projectile strike on a ~333 m Vanuatu-flag crude tanker; tradingeconomics mentions another tanker hit near Hormuz overnight into 9 Nov (no detail). UKMTO PDF (JMIC update 110, 1 Nov) could not be fetched.

items.name: War-risk premium, % of hull (latest quote, October)
items.source: Marsh/FT via House of Saud (8 Nov)
items.note: Printed as a range: 6-10% of hull value (Marsh/FT, October), vs ~0.25% pre-war; up to $20 million per supertanker voyage (Marcus Baker, Marsh). No November-dated quote found; Lloyd's List page on double-digit-million premiums could not be fetched. straits.live's own estimate: ~32x pre-crisis, set 7 Oct.

items.name: Baltic TD3C MEG-China VLCC
items.source: Baltic Exchange weekly report via Daily Cargo News
items.note: Printed: TD3C 'has fallen almost 47 points since last Friday to WS1220.63', round-trip TCE $1,303,616/day. TD15 WS564.38 ($561,731/day). Levels are as printed by the page; extraordinary by historical standards, not independently verified.

items.name: Trump to meet Qatari PM at White House as Iran diplomacy faces hurdles
items.headline: Trump to meet Qatari PM at White House as Iran diplomacy faces hurdles
items.claim: Trump meets Qatar PM/FM Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani at the White House Monday 9 Nov, closed-door; Vance also scheduled to meet him. Rubio said Sunday talks had made little progress, no imminent breakthrough, Iran's demands 'unacceptable'.

items.name: $8 billion lifeline? Iranian deal set to land on Trump's desk
items.headline: $8 billion lifeline? Iranian deal set to land on Trump's desk
items.claim: Single-outlet report citing two diplomatic sources: Iran approved a proposal to reopen Hormuz and stop attacks on Gulf shipping in return for the US lifting the naval/economic blockade and unfreezing $8bn held in Qatar; Iran reportedly dropped its demand to control the strait and collect transit fees but refuses nuclear talks. Vance/Witkoff/Kushner push it; Bessent, Lutnick, Rubio, Hegseth reportedly oppose. Not an announced deal.

items.name: Trump says renewed Iran strikes 'highly unlikely' if talks progress, warns of bridge targets
items.headline: Trump says renewed Iran strikes 'highly unlikely' if talks progress, warns of bridge targets
items.claim: Trump told CNN on Sunday 8 Nov that new strikes were 'highly unlikely' to be necessary, depending on Iran signing 'a very strong agreement'; also warned the US has identified more infrastructure targets including bridges (Israel Hayom: 38 bridges). CNBC's own 8 Nov article could not be fetched.

items.name: Rubio: Iran demands 'outrageous and ridiculous', no imminent breakthrough
items.headline: Rubio: Iran demands 'outrageous and ridiculous', no imminent breakthrough
items.claim: Rubio said Sunday 8 Nov, leaving for a G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris, that talks had made little progress and Iran's demands were unacceptable and not realistic, while Trump prefers diplomacy.

items.name: Iran FM says no negotiations since 'shock' of US midterms
items.headline: Iran FM says no negotiations since 'shock' of US midterms
items.claim: Araghchi told state TV on 8 Nov that mediators (Qatar, Pakistan named) have not traveled since the midterms and it will 'take some time'; on X he repeated the two-day Hormuz reopening offer and told Washington to accept Iran's demands or 'choose war'. No venue or date.

items.name: Araghchi speaks to 12 foreign ministers in 48h; Rezaei carried Khamenei message to Putin
items.headline: Araghchi speaks to 12 foreign ministers in 48h; Rezaei carried Khamenei message to Putin
items.claim: Araghchi said Saturday 7 Nov he had spoken with 12 foreign ministers in 48 hours incl. Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and restated seven demands; security chief Mohsen Rezaei gave Putin the same conditions and a Khamenei message in Moscow on Thursday 5 Nov.

items.name: IRGC says missile range limit lifted on Supreme Leader's order
items.headline: IRGC says missile range limit lifted on Supreme Leader's order
items.claim: IRGC spokesman Mohebbi said 7 Nov the ~2,000 km missile range cap 'has been lifted', citing Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's directive to respond with 'no geographical limits'; he also said preparations would be made if nuclear doctrine changes.

items.name: US strikes Qeshm Island; Trump calls them 'minor strikes'
items.headline: US strikes Qeshm Island; Trump calls them 'minor strikes'
items.claim: Two projectiles hit Qeshm island on the night of Friday 6 Nov, the latest of a series of strikes on Iranian air defences/launchers; Trump confirmed and called them minor. Iran's army said it downed an MQ-9 early 7 Nov. (Al Jazeera 8 Nov article dates Trump's confirmation as 'Friday, 7 November' - weekday/date mismatch in source.)

items.name: Overnight: projectiles from Sirik toward Hormuz, explosions on Qeshm; further US strike reported
items.headline: Overnight: projectiles from Sirik toward Hormuz, explosions on Qeshm; further US strike reported
items.claim: Gulf News log at 00:35 on 9 Nov: three projectiles reportedly launched from Sirik toward the strait and explosions heard on Qeshm, cause unconfirmed. Trading Economics' 9 Nov commentary says US forces reportedly struck Qeshm overnight and a tanker was hit by an unidentified projectile near Hormuz. IRNA on 7-8 Nov reported explosions on Qeshm, Jask, Sirik and Bandar Abbas (Al Jazeera).

items.name: CENTCOM disables St. Kitts-flagged cargo vessel M/V Huda in Gulf of Oman
items.headline: CENTCOM disables St. Kitts-flagged cargo vessel M/V Huda in Gulf of Oman
items.source: Al Jazeera / House of Saud / Maritime Executive
items.claim: On 7 Nov (20:35 GMT per House of Saud) a US aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of M/V Huda, which had called at an Iranian port and ignored warnings. CENTCOM cumulative since blockade reinstated 14 Jul: 147 vessels redirected, 5 merchant ships disabled (ABC called Huda the 11th; unexplained gap). CENTCOM release page itself could not be fetched.

items.name: CENTCOM stands up Task Force Iron Gate against Iran's land and Caspian supply routes
items.headline: CENTCOM stands up Task Force Iron Gate against Iran's land and Caspian supply routes
items.claim: CENTCOM announced Task Force Iron Gate (Tampa) to stop Iran moving weapons/materials over ground routes, 'reinforcing' the sea blockade (Adm. Cooper). Gulf News: White House said 9 Nov it was in full force; IRGC called it 'a play on words'. US Treasury has asked Iraq to close all but two border crossings with Iran (Arab News).

items.name: Iraq says it reached understandings with US to export oil through Hormuz via lane near Oman
items.headline: Iraq says it reached understandings with US to export oil through Hormuz via lane near Oman
items.claim: FM Fuad Hussein told Al Jazeera on 8 Nov that Iraq and the US reached understandings to allow Iraqi exports through Hormuz by a shipping lane near Oman; Iraq's war losses put at $60bn; exports ~3.5 mb/d in October vs 2.65 mb/d in September.

items.name: IRGC says two (later three; five tankers and a tug per later headline) tankers caught fire after hitting mines in Hormuz
items.headline: IRGC says two (later three; five tankers and a tug per later headline) tankers caught fire after hitting mines in Hormuz
items.source: Al Jazeera / Gulf News / House of Saud
items.claim: IRGC Navy said 7 Nov ~20:56 GMT that two tankers hit mines and burned after transiting an 'unsafe' area with navigation systems off; raised to three on 8 Nov, and a Business Recorder related headline says five tankers and a tugboat. No names, no independent confirmation; UKMTO describes one of the 7 Nov cases as a projectile strike. IRGC also warned ships against cooperating with US forces. Washington says mines were cleared.

items.name: Tanker burns 8 nm off Khasab; second tanker hit by projectile outbound (UKMTO 200-26)
items.headline: Tanker burns 8 nm off Khasab; second tanker hit by projectile outbound (UKMTO 200-26)
items.claim: Two tankers attacked in the strait on Saturday 7 Nov: one on fire NW of Khasab (crew evacuated; OSINT tentatively the ADNOC-chartered products tanker Navig8 Messi), one struck by an unknown projectile outbound, crew safe. Article says transits are roughly single to low-double digits per day.

items.name: UKMTO: 11 ships attacked in week to 4 Nov; transits 325
items.headline: UKMTO: 11 ships attacked in week to 4 Nov; transits 325
items.claim: UKMTO weekly overview: 11 attacks (8 Hormuz, 3 Arabian Gulf), 3 sunk; Hormuz transits up to 325 from 277, ~65% below pre-conflict; most AIS-broadcasting ships still using the Iranian route though more use the southern route.

items.name: Windward: crude tanker struck by projectile 6 Nov; 14 weekend crossings, 8 dark
items.headline: Windward: crude tanker struck by projectile 6 Nov; 14 weekend crossings, 8 dark
items.claim: Windward 8 Nov daily: a ~333 m Vanuatu-flag crude tanker dark since late October was hit by a projectile on 6 Nov; 14 transits from 18:00 UTC 6 Nov to 18:00 UTC 8 Nov, 8 of them dark; too early to identify a targeting pattern.

items.name: Houthis claim attack on Aramco offices in Riyadh; Saudi intercepts missiles
items.headline: Houthis claim attack on Aramco offices in Riyadh; Saudi intercepts missiles
items.source: Gulf News / Business Recorder / Iran International
items.claim: 8 Nov: Saudi-led coalition intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh; shrapnel caused minor damage to the Aramco building in the financial district, no injuries; Houthis claimed strikes on the district, Riyadh airport, Aramco tanks and Abqaiq (claims beyond the Aramco office damage unconfirmed).

items.name: Drone hits Khor Mor gas field in Iraqi Kurdistan, 2.8 GW of power lost
items.headline: Drone hits Khor Mor gas field in Iraqi Kurdistan, 2.8 GW of power lost
items.claim: A drone struck an LPG storage tank at Khor Mor on Sunday 8 Nov, fire continued into Monday, production halted and regional generation fell about 2.8 GW; no claim of responsibility.

items.name: OFAC: Iran-related designations - eight Canadian money services businesses (Operation Economic Outcast)
items.headline: OFAC: Iran-related designations - eight Canadian money services businesses (Operation Economic Outcast)
items.claim: 6 Nov: OFAC added eight Canada-based exchange/MSB entities to the SDN list under E.O. 13902 with secondary-sanctions risk notices; no general license or waiver issued. Recent-actions list shows no Iran item after 6 Nov; earlier Iran actions 4 Nov (designations, listing updates, OFAC alert) and 29 Oct (amended Iran general license), both outside gate.

items.name: Iran cannot fulfil IAEA obligations under current conditions: spokesman
items.headline: Iran cannot fulfil IAEA obligations under current conditions: spokesman
items.claim: Baqaei on 9 Nov, answering Grossi's request to visit sites: Iran remains in the NPT but cannot meet safeguards as normal after the attacks; a Bushehr inspection took place days earlier. On a reported Qatari nuclear proposal he said Iran's own two-day proposal 'remains on the table'. On 6 Nov Iran (Eslami) accused the IAEA chief of sharing information with adversaries (search snippet only).

items.name: Airlines still cancelling Saudi flights; Emirates 8 Nov Riyadh/Dammam restart scrapped
items.headline: Airlines still cancelling Saudi flights; Emirates 8 Nov Riyadh/Dammam restart scrapped
items.claim: As of 9 Nov at least 25 airlines have suspended or cut Saudi service; Emirates' planned 8 Nov restart cancelled with no new date; EASA bulletin CZIB-2026-09 in force through 16 Nov (advisory, not closure); flydubai Riyadh/Abha suspension extended to 16 Nov (search snippet).

items.name: Breakwave: more VLCCs head for the Gulf as cargoes thin
items.headline: Breakwave: more VLCCs head for the Gulf as cargoes thin
items.claim: 6 Nov: 87 VLCCs inbound to the MEG for 77 stems; 51 Far East ballasters heading to the Gulf; UKMTO had incident reports from at least five vessels since Sunday 1 Nov; a civil-defence warning near Yanbu was issued then cleared.

items.name: Stephen Miller named chief of staff (mentioned in passing)
items.headline: Stephen Miller named chief of staff (mentioned in passing)
items.claim: Al Jazeera's 7 Nov piece cites analyst Trita Parsi listing 'Stephen Miller's appointment as chief of staff' among factors raising near-term war risk; date of the appointment not given and not separately verified here. Israel Hayom 9 Nov says Hegseth faces Democratic calls for removal.
